classification.tone: Gritty, anxious, emotionally raw, and dreamlike

evaluation.positioning_hook: Sophia’s attempt to get clean collides with a black force stalking her friend group, turning one night of survival into a fight for her body, her secrets, and her future.

audience_appeal_marketability.reasoning: The core promise is easy to grasp: a teen horror story built around addiction, friendship, and a supernatural threat. The audience lane is clear, though the material is narrower than a broad four-quadrant horror play because it leans hard into intimate emotional pain and teen-group dynamics.

conceptual_hook_clarity.reasoning: The opening bathroom sequence and the black figure give the script an immediate horror engine, and Sophia’s struggle with pills adds a strong personal pressure. The concept lands, but the mythology and the exact rules of the force stay impressionistic rather than sharply defined.

character_appeal_and_long_term_potential.reasoning: Sophia has a compelling central contradiction: she is trying to survive both a supernatural event and a family system that keeps her off balance. The friend group has warmth and chemistry, but most supporting players function more as emotional satellites than as fully independent engines.

creative_originality_and_boldness.reasoning: The script’s strongest move is fusing teen social life, recovery imagery, and occult dread into one emotional field, especially in the mirror, pill bottle, and foaming-mouth imagery. The voice is willing to be strange and subjective, which gives it a more personal identity than a standard possession setup.

narrative_momentum_engagement.reasoning: The opening has urgency, and the group scenes keep the energy moving, but the middle section becomes more episodic as the story cycles through locations and visions. The climax is emotionally charged, yet the escalation is more atmospheric than tightly causal.

resonant_originality.reasoning: The script feels like a familiar horror framework filtered through a specific emotional wound, which makes the material feel both legible and personal. The recurring pills, mirrors, blackout imagery, and social-media/texting texture give it a fresh surface that still reads immediately.

world_density_and_texture.reasoning: The school, home, diner, amusement park, and forest create a recognizable teen-world ecosystem with enough social detail to feel lived in. The world is more intimate than expansive, but the family tension, friend-group rituals, and school artifacts give it useful texture.

tonal_specificity.reasoning: The tone blends teen intimacy, domestic discomfort, and supernatural panic in a way that feels distinct from cleaner, more polished horror packaging. The script is most specific when it lets ordinary teen behavior sit right next to dread, like the joking, kissing, and texting under the shadow of the black figure.

latent_depth_slow_burn_potential.reasoning: There are clear reserves beneath the surface: recovery, family control, queer/romantic tension, and the possibility that the horror is tied to Sophia’s internal state. The draft hints at that depth more than it fully organizes it, but the ingredients are there for a richer feature pass.

relationship_density_and_ensemble_engine.reasoning: The friend group has a real social web, and the scenes of teasing, kissing, and mutual support create usable ensemble energy. Still, the story remains anchored primarily to Sophia and Jade, with several other characters serving the main arc rather than generating their own independent momentum.

casting_characteristics: One central female lead role with strong emotional range

locations.interior_exterior_ratio: Mostly interior with some exterior day/night inserts

technical.vfx_details: Black figure appearances, darkness swallowing effects, flickering lights, and a few supernatural visual moments.
technical.sfx_needs: Practical blood splatter, electrocution beat, foaming mouth makeup, darkness/possession effects.

rights_flags.detail: Vape is prominently featured as a prop and behavioral marker.

platform_fit.series_engine_or_release_model: Feature release model with festival-to-platform potential

cost.note: Contemporary teen horror with contained interiors, a few exteriors, and minor VFX sits in a modest feature budget lane.

cast.note: The ensemble is youth-heavy and benefits from chemistry across multiple friend-group roles, with one central lead and several supporting teens.

location.note: The story moves through a house, school, diner, amusement park, forest, hospital, and car interiors, with several night setups.

content.note: Pills, self-destructive behavior, blood, electrocution, and supernatural body-horror imagery keep it in a mature horror lane.

rights.note: No real people, music, or IP-heavy references drive the story; the main clearance note is the visible vape prop.

strengths.dimension_or_area: Sophia is built around a strong contradiction.
strengths.what_it_means: That gives a lead actress a role with addiction, fear, defiance, and tenderness all in the same frame, which is exactly the kind of part that can anchor a festival-facing horror feature. Young dramatic leads and horror buyers looking for a performance-first centerpiece will see the value immediately.
strengths.evidence: The opening pill sequence, the bathroom mirror beat, and the later confrontation with her parents all place Sophia in emotional conflict before the horror fully lands.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The horror is tied to recovery imagery.
strengths.what_it_means: That creates a commercial hook beyond standard teen possession material because the supernatural threat is braided into a recognizable personal struggle. Buyers chasing elevated horror and audiences drawn to psychologically loaded genre pieces will respond to that overlap.
strengths.evidence: Pills coming back up in the sink, the “SPARE” bottles, the foaming mouth, and the repeated bathroom imagery all build the same symbolic lane.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The friend group has real social chemistry.
strengths.what_it_means: The ensemble gives the movie a built-in emotional engine, so the horror is happening to a group the audience already wants to stay with. That makes the script attractive to producers who want a castable teen ensemble and to buyers who know friendship dynamics help horror travel.
strengths.evidence: The bedroom pillow fight, the diner texting sequence, the teasing, the kissing, and the group ritual around the orb all show a lived-in circle.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The tone mixes intimacy with dread.
strengths.what_it_means: That tonal blend gives the project a lane between raw character drama and supernatural horror, which is a useful place for streamers and indie genre labels. Directors who like performance-forward horror with emotional texture will see a lot to work with here.
strengths.evidence: The script moves from joking in a bedroom to locked doors, flickering lights, and a body being swallowed by darkness without losing the emotional thread.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The visual motifs are easy to market.
strengths.what_it_means: Mirrors, black figures, foaming mouths, and darkness swallowing bodies are clean horror images that can carry a trailer and poster campaign. Genre buyers and marketing teams can sell this off a few strong frames.
strengths.evidence: The mirror/calendar sequence, the window figure, the blackout attacks, and the hospital-room swallow beat all create repeatable iconography.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The family conflict gives the story a second engine.
strengths.what_it_means: The parents, sister, and custody-adjacent paperwork add a domestic pressure line that can widen the emotional appeal beyond the horror premise. That makes the script more attractive to buyers who want genre material with a human core and to actors who want scenes that play outside the scare set pieces.
strengths.evidence: The certificate for Bonnie and Ryan French, the tense bedroom confrontation, and the sister’s presence all point to a larger family system around Sophia.

whats_special.headline: This is a performance-forward teen horror feature with a clear emotional engine: a girl trying to get clean while a black force turns her friend group, her family, and her own body into the battleground. The script’s best asset is that it doesn’t just stage scares — it gives producers a lead role, a friend-group ensemble, and a visual language that can sell in one glance.

lead_characters.name: Jade
lead_characters.hook: Jade is the most emotionally open member of the group, the one who can pivot from joking and physical affection to deep concern without feeling false. She reads as the friend who notices everything and the person most likely to become the story’s emotional bridge when the group starts to fracture.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role Florence Pugh had in Midsommar — emotionally legible, physically present, and asked to carry both intimacy and dread in the same frame. Actors who want a part that plays warmth, loyalty, and mounting fear without disappearing into the ensemble will want this.

lead_characters.name: Emma
lead_characters.hook: Emma has a brittle, funny, slightly volatile energy that makes her feel like a real friend-group pressure point. She’s the kind of character who can turn a room with one line, then reveal fear or hurt underneath the joke.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of supporting showcase Kaitlyn Dever has repeatedly made memorable — a sharp, emotionally readable role that can steal scenes through timing and vulnerability. Young actors who want a scene-stealing ensemble part with room for humor and panic will be drawn to her.

lead_characters.name: Sam
lead_characters.hook: Sam is quieter and more reactive, but that makes her useful as an emotional barometer inside the group. She helps sell the sense that these girls have history, and her presence gives the ensemble a softer, more observant texture.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role that lets an actor do the subtle ensemble work seen in The Virgin Suicides — present, watchful, and emotionally specific without needing speeches. Actors who excel at contained reactions and group chemistry will see the appeal.

lead_characters.name: Maddy
lead_characters.hook: Maddy feels like the steadier friend, someone who can hold the group together even as the situation gets stranger. She has a grounded presence that helps the script keep one foot in ordinary teen life.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of grounded ensemble part that gives an actor the reliability and emotional clarity seen in supporting turns from It Follows. Performers who like playing the calm center in a group under siege will respond to it.

lead_characters.name: Nancy
lead_characters.hook: Nancy has an alert, watchful quality and seems tuned to danger before the others are. She’s one of the characters who helps the horror feel communal, because she reacts like someone who can sense the room changing.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role that gives an actor the nervous intelligence of a supporting player in Scream — quick reactions, group authority, and a few moments that can land hard. Actors who want a sharp teen-horror utility role with personality will like it.

lead_characters.name: Kyle
lead_characters.hook: Kyle is the boyfriend energy in the group, flirtatious and socially fluent, but not just a placeholder. He helps define the romantic and social web around Sophia, which gives the ensemble a more lived-in feel.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role that gives a young actor the easy charm and relationship texture of a supporting player in The Perks of Being a Wallflower. It’s a useful part for someone who can play chemistry, teasing, and a little emotional ambiguity.

lead_characters.name: Bryan
lead_characters.hook: Bryan is another social node in the group, more playful and physically present than deeply interior on the page. He helps keep the friend circle active and gives the ensemble more movement and pairings.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the sort of ensemble role that lets an actor play the loose, social energy of a teen-horror supporting part like the guys in Bodies Bodies Bodies. It’s a good fit for someone who can make a small role feel plugged into the group’s chemistry.

lead_characters.name: Nate
lead_characters.hook: Nate functions as part of the social fabric and the missing-person pressure in the middle of the story. Even with limited page time, he helps create the sense that the group’s world extends beyond the room.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of compact teen role that can still register if played with the deadpan unease of a supporting part in Fear Street. Actors looking for a memorable, low-page-count genre credit would see the utility.

lead_characters.name: Phoebe
lead_characters.hook: Phoebe is one of the group’s connective figures, helping move scenes and keep the ensemble in motion. She adds to the sense that this is a real friend circle rather than a two-person story with extras.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of ensemble support role that gives an actor the social specificity of a teen part in Booksmart. It’s a good fit for someone who can make a few beats feel fully lived-in.

lead_characters.name: Tina
lead_characters.hook: Tina pops in with attitude and a sharp edge, which helps the group feel less uniform. She gives the script another distinct teen voice in the mix.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of scene-sized role that lets an actor do the fast, memorable work seen in horror ensembles like Scream. It’s a clean opportunity for someone who can land a line and leave a mark.

lead_characters.name: Jade's Mom / Tori
lead_characters.hook: Tori carries the domestic side of the story, moving between tenderness, grief, and the kind of parental control that can feel loving and suffocating at once. She gives the film a grounded adult presence that broadens the emotional field beyond the teen group.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role that gives an actress the domestic intensity of Amy Ryan in Gone Baby Gone — a parent whose love and pressure are both legible in the same scene. Mid-career dramatic actresses looking for a contained but emotionally loaded supporting part will chase it.

lead_characters.name: Sophia's Mom
lead_characters.hook: Sophia’s mom is controlling, defensive, and emotionally volatile, but she’s not written as a simple villain; she’s part of the family system that keeps Sophia trapped. The role has sharp edges and a lot of room for tension in very little space.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role that gives an actress the combustible domestic authority of Laura Linney in The Savages — a parent whose love is inseparable from conflict. Actors who like playing complicated maternal pressure will be drawn to it.

lead_characters.name: Sophia's Dad
lead_characters.hook: Sophia’s dad is quieter and more exhausted, which makes him feel like the family’s emotional aftershock rather than its engine. He adds texture to the home life and helps the parents feel like a unit with its own history.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of restrained supporting role that gives an actor the weary, lived-in quality of a parent in Manchester by the Sea. Character actors who can do a lot with a few lines and a look will find it appealing.

lead_characters.name: Ruth
lead_characters.hook: Ruth is the emotional relief valve in the story, a golden retriever whose presence softens the room and gives Sophia one uncomplicated source of affection. She also helps mark the domestic world as something worth saving.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is a strong animal role in the sense that it gives the film a memorable emotional anchor and a clean visual motif. Animal handlers and producers know a dog like Ruth can become a trailer-friendly image and a sympathy lever.

director_appeal.hook: A director who wants to make horror feel personal, not mechanical.
director_appeal.fit_profile: First- or second-feature directors, or established indie filmmakers moving into genre, who already care about performance-forward storytelling, subjective dread, and domestic realism. This material rewards directors who can stage fear through behavior, texture, and emotional pressure rather than through big set-piece spectacle.
director_appeal.detail: The movie gives a director a chance to build scares out of mirrors, bedrooms, hallways, and group dynamics, which is a very different craft lane from effects-heavy horror. It will attract filmmakers who want to prove they can make a contained genre piece feel intimate, stylish, and actor-driven.

buyer_appeal.lane: Streaming horror / indie genre lane with elevated emotional stakes
buyer_appeal.detail: It is contained enough to package around a strong newcomer or rising young lead rather than requiring a major star, and the teen-horror lane remains one of the most reliable discovery zones for streamers and specialty distributors. The contemporary setting, modest effects load, and clear trailer imagery make it exportable and easy to market off mood, cast chemistry, and a single central performance.

considerations.detail: The black figure, the orb, the darkness attacks, and the hospital-room voice all create a strong mood, and a next pass could clarify the rules just enough to sharpen the feature engine. What would it look like if one or two cause-and-effect anchors were made explicit earlier, so the escalation feels as inevitable as it is eerie?

The amusement park, pool, diner, and forest beats each add texture, but they read more like adjacent episodes than a single tightening chain. One lever would be to connect those beats through a clearer objective or countdown so each stop changes the situation rather than simply extending it.

considerations.area: The ensemble could carry more independent weight.
considerations.detail: The friend group chemistry is already doing good work, and the version of the script where one or two supporting characters have a sharper personal stake would deepen the ensemble engine. That would give the movie more combinatorial energy without changing the core premise.

considerations.area: The family thread is a valuable simplification lever.
considerations.detail: The parents, sister, custody paperwork, and home tension all point to a strong domestic lane, and the version of the script where those elements are concentrated into fewer scenes could protect momentum while keeping the emotional spine intact. That would also help the feature stay in a contained production footprint without losing the story’s human core.

considerations.area: The night footprint is the main production load.
considerations.detail: Most of the horror language lives in night interiors and exterior night beats, so the schedule will want to be built around efficient company moves and controlled lighting setups. That is still very manageable for this tier, but it is the main place where planning will protect the budget.
